cues.en: And, based on how modern king crabs live, scientists think that Paralomis probably lived

cues.en: They turned into false crabs!!

cues.en: So why does this keep happening?

cues.en: What is it about the crab’s form that makes it so evolutionarily successful -- so successful

cues.en: that non-crabs are apparently jealous of it?

cues.en: Well, it might sound odd to say this about an animal with a shell, but the answer seems

cues.en: to be that it’s all about flexibility.

cues.en: Crab-like creatures date back to the Late Devonian Period, about 365 million years ago.

cues.en: lobsters, and crabs -- both true and false.

cues.zh: 而古古虾是迄今发现最古老的类似龙虾的十足目动物，也是最古老的

cues.zh: 进食附肢，用于在柔软的海底泥中觅食。

cues.en: But then, around 260 million years ago, decapods split into two groups -- the Anomurans, or

cues.zh: 那些假的、冒充螃蟹的家伙，以及短尾类，即真蟹——那些
cues.en: those false, fake wanna-be crabs, and the Brachyurans, or the true crabs -- the crabs

cues.zh: 没有骗你的蟹。
cues.en: that aren’t lying to you.

cues.en: The oldest undisputed true crab is Eoprosopon, a crustacean that lived 185 million years

cues.zh: 的早侏罗世。
cues.en: ago in the early Jurassic Period.

cues.en: And, for a while, scientists argued over whether it actually belonged in the crab family, because

cues.zh: 它有些特征不像蟹，比如腹部稍微更长一些，还有非常
cues.en: it has some un-crab-like traits — like a slightly more elongated abdomen and really

cues.zh: 显眼的触角。
cues.en: prominent antennae.

cues.zh: 不过，专家用新的成像技术重新评估了唯一已知的标本后，认定
cues.en: But after re-evaluating the only known specimen with new imaging techniques, experts decided

cues.zh: Eoprosopon 是短尾下目非常早期的一员。
cues.en: that Eoprosopon was a very early member of the Brachyura.

cues.zh: 而在十足目演化树的另一端，还有 Platykotta，它比 Eoprosopon 稍微

cues.zh: 古老一些，距今约 2 亿年，生活在晚三叠世。
cues.en: older than Eoprosopon at about 200 million years old, from the late Triassic Period.

cues.zh: 它被认为是最古老的假蟹，外形更像龙虾。
cues.en: It’s thought to be the oldest false crab, and it looked more like a lobster.

cues.zh: 但在漫长的进化过程中，异尾下目和短尾下目都逐渐演化成
cues.en: But over the course of evolutionary time, both the Anomurans and the Brachyurans came

cues.zh: 我们今天熟悉的“螃蟹形态”。
cues.en: closer and closer to what we think of as the “crab shape” that we know today.

cues.zh: 这两个类群里，甲壳类动物一次又一次地从龙虾那样细长的身体开始演化。
cues.en: In both groups, time and time again, a crustacean started out with the elongated body of a lobster

cues.zh: 最终演化成更圆、更扁的螃蟹形状。
cues.en: only to evolve into the rounder, flatter shape of a crab.

cues.zh: 科学家们一百多年来一直在试图弄清楚这是为什么
cues.en: And scientists have been trying to figure out why this happens for more than a hundred
years.

cues.zh: 最早认识到这一点的博物学家之一，是一位名叫 Lancelot 的英国动物学家，
cues.en: One of the first naturalists to recognize this was an English zoologist named Lancelot

cues.zh: Alexander Borradaile。
cues.en: Alexander Borradaile.

cues.zh: 1916 年，他将这一过程命名为“螃蟹化”，意思是变得像螃蟹。
cues.en: And in 1916 he named the process “carcinization,” which means to become crab-like.

cues.zh: 他还描述了自己认为这一过程是如何发生的。
cues.en: And he also described how he thought the process happened.

cues.zh: 简单来说，龙虾那条长长的“尾巴”——也叫腹部——会随着时间推移逐渐变短，
cues.en: Basically, the long “tail” of a lobster, called a pleon, grows shorter over time and

cues.zh: 并收拢到身体下面。
cues.en: gets tucked under the body.

cues.zh: 与此同时，龙虾前端狭窄的头胸甲变得越来越宽，
cues.en: And, at the same time, the narrow front part of the lobster - the carapace - grows wider

cues.zh: 越来越扁，直到最后看起来就像我们所说的螃蟹。
cues.en: and flatter, until it eventually winds up looking like what we’d call a crab.

cues.zh: 好吧，但这到底是为——什么呢？为什么这些动物会一再从狭长变得又扁
cues.en: OK, so, but whyyyy would these animals repeatedly go from being long and narrow to flat and

cues.zh: 又圆？
cues.en: round?

cues.zh: 早在 20 世纪 80 年代，有一项研究分析了整个中生代
cues.en: Well, back in the 1980s, a study analyzed all of the fossil crustaceans throughout the

cues.zh: 的所有甲壳类化石，发现蟹状甲壳动物
cues.en: whole Mesozoic Era, and discovered that there was an explosion of crab-shaped crustaceans

cues.zh: 在这个时期出现了爆发式增长。
cues.en: during this span of time.

cues.zh: 另一项更新的研究发现，这种现象在白垩纪
cues.en: Another, more recent study found that this phenomenon really took off during the Cretaceous

cues.zh: 迎来了真正的大爆发，专家有时称之为“白垩纪螃蟹革命”，或者如果你喜欢的话，也可以叫“中生代
cues.en: Period, which experts sometimes call the Cretaceous Crab Revolution or, if you prefer, the Mesozoic

cues.en: Decapod Revolution.

cues.en: Both of those are available!

cues.en: Nearly 80 percent of the major groups of true crabs that we know of today originated in

cues.zh: 这一时期。
cues.en: this period.

cues.zh: 在整个中生代，多样性出现了长期转变，朝着更多
cues.en: And throughout the Mesozoic Era, there was a long-term shift in diversity toward more

cues.zh: 蟹形物种发展，尤其是朝着真蟹发展，而远离长体形物种。
cues.en: crab-shaped species, specifically toward true crabs, and away from long-bodied ones.

cues.zh: 这些类似蟹的生物似乎还利用了更多不同种类的栖息地，
cues.en: The crab-like creatures also seemed to have exploited many more different kinds of habitats

cues.zh: 比它们更像龙虾的亲戚要多得多。
cues.en: than their more lobster-y relatives.

cues.zh: 一个可能的解释是，它们的形状带来了更强的移动能力。
cues.en: One possible explanation for this is that their shape allowed for greater mobility.

cues.zh: 蟹类更圆、更扁的形状，让它们能更高效地行走、奔跑、游泳和挖洞。
cues.en: The rounder, flatter shape of crabs lets crabs walk, run, swim and burrow more efficiently.

cues.zh: 甚至还有会爬树的蟹，这简直是另一种专属的噩梦素材！
cues.en: There are even crabs that climb tree, which is its own special kind of nightmare fuel!

cues.zh: 相比之下，外形更像龙虾或虾的动物，往往局限于
cues.en: By contrast, animals that are shaped more like lobsters or shrimp are often limited

cues.zh: 游泳、挖洞或在地面上快速爬行。
cues.en: to just swimming, burrowing, or scuttling on the ground.

cues.zh: 其他研究人员认为，变成螃蟹形状是生物更好地
cues.en: Other researchers say the transformation to a crab shape was a way for organisms to better

cues.zh: 躲避捕食者的一种方式。
cues.en: evade predators.

cues.zh: 通过失去腹部——那条长尾巴——它们就少了一个捕食者
cues.en: By losing the pleon—that long tail—they had one less delicious appendage that predators

cues.zh: 可能抓住的美味附肢。
cues.en: might grab onto.

cues.zh: 所以，既然螃蟹形状让甲壳类动物能去更多地方、做更多事、躲避
cues.en: So, since the crab shape allowed crustaceans to go more places, do more things, and evade

cues.zh: 更多捕食者，这种形状就随着时间被选择保留下来，许多细长的甲壳类动物
cues.en: more predators, that shape was selected for over time, and lots of elongated crustaceans

cues.zh: 逐渐变得像螃蟹——即使它们并不是螃蟹。
cues.en: came to be shaped like crabs—even if they weren’t crabs.

cues.zh: 但当然，有时候某些适应——不管看起来多么有用——就是
cues.en: But of course, sometimes certain adaptations -- no matter how helpful they might seem -- just

cues.zh: 没能延续下来。
cues.en: don’t stick.

cues.zh: 而且，为了让事情更有趣！甲壳类动物有很多次失去了
cues.en: And, just to keep things interesting!, there have been many times when crustaceans lost

cues.zh: 它们类似螃蟹的形状！
cues.en: their crab-like shape!

cues.zh: 这被称为，你猜对了，去蟹化。

cues.zh: 这种现象在真正的螃蟹中也出现过，比如一种叫 Callichimaera perplexa 的化石蟹
cues.en: This has happened among true crabs, like in a fossil crab called Callichimaera perplexa

cues.en: Its name means “perplexing beautiful chimera” and it lived between 95 million and 90 million

cues.zh: 身体形状也跟我们通常想象的……螃蟹样不太一样。
cues.en: its body shape wasn’t quite the same as what we normally think of as … crabby.

cues.zh: 我是说，你看看这双眼睛！
cues.en: I mean look at this things eyes!

cues.zh: 简直是螃蟹界的尤达宝宝。
cues.en: It’s like the Baby Yoda of crabs

cues.zh: 总而言之，蟹化现象是趋同演化中比较迷人的例子之一。
cues.en: All told, the phenomenon of carcinization is one of the more fascinating examples of

cues.zh: 趋同演化。
cues.en: convergent evolution.

cues.zh: 甲壳类动物演化成螃蟹形状的原因有很多，即使它
cues.en: There are a lot of reasons a crustacean might evolve into the shape of a crab, even if it’s

cues.zh: 并不是真正的螃蟹：这种形态能让它在运动和生活方式上有很大的灵活性。
cues.en: not actually a crab: It allows for a lot of versatility in locomotion and lifestyle.

cues.zh: 如今，螃蟹能在深海中攀爬、在海滩上飞奔、在沙子里打洞，
cues.en: Today, crabs can clamber around the deep sea, scuttle over beaches, burrow in the sand,

cues.zh: 还能在水中推动自己游动。
cues.en: and propel themselves through the water.

cues.zh: 它们生活在淡水、咸水以及陆地上——几乎无处不在，
cues.en: They live in freshwater, salt water, and on land — they’re pretty much everywhere,

cues.zh: 无论是真蟹还是假蟹都是如此。
cues.en: true crabs and false alike.

cues.zh: 归根结底，这一切都取决于生物能否在环境中良好生存。
cues.en: At the end of the day, it’s all about how well an organism can survive in its environment.

cues.zh: 所以，我们或许也不能怪假蟹为什么都想变成螃蟹。
cues.en: So maybe we can’t blame for false crabs for wanting to be crabs.
